definitions.explanation: Small enough to be eaten in a single bite — used to describe food portioned so the whole piece fits comfortably in the mouth at once. Frequently seen on food packaging, in recipes, and on menus to signal easy, tidy eating.

examples.japanese: {一口|ひとくち}サイズ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧チョコ。
⟦チーズ→チーズ：00026_chiizu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{一口|ひとくち}サイズ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{切|き}って→切る：02693_kiru⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please cut the cheese into bite-sized pieces.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}ども⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{食|た}べやすい→食べやすい：21799_tabeyasui⟧よう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、⟦おにぎり→おにぎり：04956_onigiri⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{一口|ひとくち}サイズ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{握|にぎ}った→握る：02383_nigiru⟧。
examples.english: I made the rice balls bite-sized so that the children could eat them easily.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{一口|ひとくち}→一口：10474_hitokuchi⟧ (one mouthful, one bite) and ⟦サイズ→サイズ：01363_saizu⟧ (size, from English). Describes food or pieces of food that are small enough to fit in the mouth in one bite — a common size indicator on packaged snacks, in recipes, and on party menus.

USAGE:
- Typically modifies a noun with ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧: {一口|ひとくち}サイズ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ゼリー→ゼリー：11025_zerii⟧ (bite-sized jelly).
- With ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{切|き}る→切る：02693_kiru⟧ / ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{分|わ}ける→分ける：02333_wakeru⟧ it means to cut or divide something into bite-sized pieces.
- Common in marketing copy because it signals convenience and tidy, mess-free eating.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一口|ひとくち}サイズ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧チョコ: bite-sized chocolate
- {一口|ひとくち}サイズ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ケーキ→ケーキ：01356_keeki⟧: bite-sized cake
- {一口|ひとくち}サイズ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{切|き}る→切る：02693_kiru⟧: to cut into bite-sized pieces
- {一口|ひとくち}サイズ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{丸|まる}める→丸める：11313_marumeru⟧: to roll into bite-sized balls
- ⟦{食|た}べやすい→食べやすい：21799_tabeyasui⟧{一口|ひとくち}サイズ: easy-to-eat bite-size

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{一口|ひとくち}→一口：10474_hitokuchi⟧: one mouthful, one bite — the base noun; can refer to a single bite of food or a single sip
- ⟦{小|こ}→小〜：00240_ko⟧⟦サイズ→サイズ：01363_saizu⟧: small size — about overall size rather than eating in one bite
- ミニサイズ: mini size — small version, not specifically about biting
